definition: Installed workstation products using local files, operating-system integration, packaging, and upgrade behavior.
counterexample: A browser-only dashboard with no local filesystem or desktop distribution needs.
nonGoals: Do not overwrite user files without recoverable backups.
Do not promise OS support that is not exercised.

requiredDecisions.question: Which operating systems and architectures are supported?
Which filesystem locations and file formats are authoritative?
How are upgrades, rollback, and data recovery handled?
Which repository and branch policy are authoritative?
Who may approve promotion, merge, migration, deployment, and publication?
What rollback restores code, data, and external side effects?

requirements: Use atomic or recoverable writes for user-owned files.
Handle missing, locked, malformed, and externally modified files.
Package and update the application on declared operating systems.
verifications: Run filesystem failure and recovery fixtures.
Test packaging and upgrade on each declared OS.
Verify data remains readable across supported versions.
authority: Resolution creates a candidate specification only; factory-ready, dispatch, merge, migration, deployment, publication, and courseware release require explicit human authority.
